item.title: Natchez unveils second historical marker honoring Prince Abdul Rahman Ibrahima - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NATCHEZ — The City of Natchez unveiled a historical marker Wednesday honoring Prince Abdul Rahman Ibrahima on Silver Street, near the site where he arrived as an enslaved man in 1788 and later departed as a free man in 1828.

Shabilla Adams, left, and Beverly Adams are direct descendants of Prince Abdul Rahman Ibrahima. They are pictured at the new marker on Silver Street. Photo by Roscoe Barnes III

City officials said the marker commemorates Ibrahima’s journey from enslavement to freedom and highlights his connection to Natchez’s history. The marker stands near the riverfront location where he and his wife, Isabella, left Natchez on April 8, 1828.

Shelia Byrd, deputy director of the Programs and Communication Division at the Mississippi Department of Archives and History and a former Associated Press reporter, spoke during the ceremony. Byrd said the marker reflects Natchez’s willingness to acknowledge the full scope of its history, including difficult chapters tied to slavery.

Ibrahima was a Muslim prince from Timbo in the Futa Jallon region of present-day Guinea in West Africa. According to the city, he was captured in battle in 1788, sold to slave traders and endured 40 years of enslavement on Thomas Foster’s plantation near Natchez before gaining his freedom.

Mayor Dan Gibson said the city has a responsibility to tell the full story of those who helped build Natchez. He said Ibrahima’s story represents not only one man’s life but also the broader history of enslaved people whose labor shaped the community.

The Silver Street marker is the second historical marker in the Natchez-Adams County area honoring Ibrahima. The first was unveiled in October 2025 on Highway 61 North near Historic Jefferson College and focuses on his 1807 meeting with Dr. John Coates Cox. City officials said the new marker emphasizes his West African roots and the site of his departure to freedom.

item.title: JSU murder trial of Randall Smith ends in mistrial. What to know - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Pam Dankins The Clarion-Ledger

Following days of testimony, Hinds County Circuit Court Judge Adrienne Wooten declared a mistrial April 9 in the murder trial of Randall Smith, who is accused of shooting and killing his Jackson State University roommate Flynn Brown in 2022.

Smith is charged with first-degree murder in the Dec. 2, 2022, death of Brown on Jackson State’s campus. Smith, 20 at the time, was on trial for murdering Brown, 22, after an altercation began over doughnuts.

Smith of New Orleans and Brown of New Jersey were suitemates living on the seventh floor of the John W. Dixon Residence Hall on Jackson State’s campus.

A Hinds County jury deliberated for more than three hours April 9 but failed to reach a unanimous decision. A mistrial was declared by Wooten.

After court, Smith was taken back to the Hinds County jail. Prosecutors will now decide whether they want to try the case again.

Following is a recap of everything we know leading up to the judge’s ruling:

Why was a mistrial declared? The jury deliberated for roughly three hours and 30 minutes April 9 before they sent a note to Wooten stating they could not reach a verdict.

When polled by Wooten, 11 of 12 jurors stated that further deliberations would not assist them with returning a verdict. When Wooten asked if returning to court the next day would assist with arriving at a unanimous verdict, at least three jurors said they were “willing to try.”

Wooten said the court is not in a position to force a jury to arrive at a decision, but it certainly has an obligation to try to determine what direction it must go in as it relates to furthering deliberation or granting a mistrial.

“Based off of what has taken place here on tonight, the court is going to grant a mistrial,” Wooten said.

After the mistrial, jurors spoke to media outlets saying all 12 members believed Smith was guilty but disagreed if Smith was guilty of first-degree murder or a lesser charge such as second-degree murder or manslaughter.

How did Flynn Brown’s family react to mistrial? Following the ruling, Flynn Brown’s mother, Michele Hill-Brown, and Flynn’s father, Michael Brown, both spoke to reporters saying that they are not going to stop fighting for justice for her son.

“We will get justice for Flynn. … (Smith) was jealous of my son in every way: his athleticism, his personality, his friendliness, his kind heart,” Michele said. “We’re going to get justice. It’s not over.”

Brown was an only child.

“You send your kid from Jersey all the way here,” Michael said. “He gets murdered, slaughtered. And then you can’t find a jury that can just understand the questions or whatever. So, what kind of system are we living in? It’s not fair. You know when I’m going to see my son? When I’m dead, in my grave.”

Defense response to mistrial After the ruling, defense attorney Kevin Dale Camp spoke to reporters April 9, saying they had hoped to get an acquittal on the case but would “T-up and do it again.” Camp also shared Smith was “disappointed” by the ruling.

“This is hard on him and his family a lot, and I think they want some closure,” Camp said. “That didn’t happen. We’ll have to figure it out a different way.”

What did Smith say in his confession to shooting Brown? During the trial, the jury listened to a recording of Smith confessing to killing Brown, stuffing Brown’s body into a storage box and dragging it outside. Once outside, Smith dumped the body inside Brown’s Dodge Challenger.

The recording also gave insight into Smith’s version of events leading up to the murder of Brown. Smith said he was eating donuts when Brown took them, leading to a fight where Brown choked him. During the struggle, Smith recalled Brown had a gun in a drawer, retrieved it and fatally shot Brown.

Smith also admitted to changing clothes and cleaning the bloody scene with bleach. Smith maintained the killing was in self-defense.

What did state, defense say to jurors in closing? Hinds County Assistant District Attorney Briana Keeler urged jurors to focus on the evidence and reject what she outlined as a web of lies spun by Smith.

Keeler said Smith lied about the incident, tried to dispose of the body and cleaned the crime scene with bleach instead of calling 911.

“Bleach is not the smell of fear,” Keeler said. “Bleach is not the smell of panic. Bleach is certainly not the smell of self-defense. That’s the smell of someone trying to erase what happened, someone trying to cover up what they did.”

The defense argued Smith removed Brown’s body and cleaned the room, believing it was the right action at the time.

“All the information that has been brought, points to one thing: that it was self-defense. (Prosecutors) have not shown that he did anything that would have negated that,” Camp said.

Pam Dankins is the breaking news reporter for the Clarion Ledger. Have a tip? Email her at [email protected] .

item.title: Tupelo police arrest man months after felony fleeing crash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – Tupelo police have arrested a man in connection with a felony fleeing case that began with a traffic stop attempt in November and ended in a crash.

According to the Tupelo Police Department, officers on Nov. 7, 2025, tried to stop a black Toyota Camry near Ida B. Wells Street and Enoch Avenue for an equipment violation.

Police said the vehicle then began driving erratically, ran stop signs and continued fleeing from officers. Authorities said the chase ended when the vehicle crashed into another vehicle and the people inside ran away on foot.

Investigators later identified the driver as 25-year-old Earnest Long Jr. of Tupelo.

Police said Long was arrested April 2, 2026, and charged with felony fleeing.

At an April 3 hearing, Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Willie Allen ordered Long held on a $15,000 bond.

item.title: Pickle Fest Returns to Jackson in June - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Agriculture & Forestry Museum Foundation will host its 6th Annual Pickle Fest on June 13-14 at the Mississippi Agriculture & Forestry Museum, offering two days of food, entertainment and family-friendly activities celebrating Mississippi’s agricultural heritage.

The festival will run from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. June 13 and noon to 5 p.m. June 14 at the museum, located at 1150 Lakeland Drive. Organizers said tickets are on sale now and expected to sell out following a record turnout of 7,200 attendees from 24 states in 2025.

Admission is $10 per day for foundation members and $15 per day for non-members, while children under 3 are admitted free. A separate ticket is required for each day.

Pickle Fest will feature live music, educational demonstrations and pickle-inspired foods throughout the museum grounds and its Small Town Mississippi exhibit. Proceeds from the event will benefit the Mississippi Agriculture & Forestry Museum and the National Agricultural Aviation Museum.

Festival highlights include a pickle eating contest, a new pickle-themed costume contest, and competitions for homemade pickled creations and dishes featuring pickled ingredients. A children’s area will offer crafts, story time, face painting and take-home cucumber seeds.

The Mississippi State Extension Service will also host pickling demonstrations, alongside vendors offering Mississippi-made products.

Dr. Bill Herndon, chair of the foundation’s board, said the event continues to grow each year and brings together the community and businesses around a shared interest. Museum Executive Director Theresa Love said the festival serves as both a celebration and an educational opportunity highlighting the state’s agriculture and agricultural aviation history.

Named “Best Small Festival in Mississippi” by the Mississippi Tourism Association, Pickle Fest emphasizes food traditions, fermentation and the state’s agricultural legacy.

More information, including sponsorship, vendor and volunteer opportunities, is available online. The sponsor deadline is May 8, and the vendor deadline is April 17.

item.title: Natchez Trace Parkway to Close Double Arch Bridge for Construction Through 2027 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
TUPELO — The Natchez Trace Parkway will close the Double Arch Bridge near Nashville beginning April 15 for construction of a permanent pedestrian safety barrier, officials announced.

The bridge will be closed to motor vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists until spring 2027, according to the National Park Service.

During construction, a portion of the parkway between Big Tree Overlook at milepost 440 and the Highway 96 off-ramp at milepost 437 will also be closed. Officials said a 7.5-mile detour route will be in place, with additional travel information available online and through parkway social media channels.

“Visitor safety is our top priority,” Superintendent Wendy Ross said in a statement. “This project is an important step in ensuring the Double Arch Bridge continues to be a safe and welcoming place for everyone who visits the Natchez Trace Parkway.”

The project will replace a temporary barrier with a permanent structure designed to be more durable, effective and visually appealing. Crews will also perform preventative maintenance on the bridge, including repainting.

Officials advised bicyclists planning long-distance rides to park at the Highway 96 off-ramp and travel south of milepost 437. For shorter rides, cyclists can park at milepost 442 and ride to Big Tree Overlook and back.

Completed in 1994, the 1,572-foot Double Arch Bridge spans Birdsong Hollow at a height of about 155 feet. It was the first segmentally constructed concrete arch bridge in the United States and received the 1995 Presidential Award for Design Excellence. The structure is also considered eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places due to its engineering and design.

item.title: Jones County deputies search for man who failed to appear for meth trafficking trial - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – The Jones County Sheriff’s Department is asking for the public’s help in locating a man who failed to appear in circuit court for trial.

Authorities said 45-year-old Darrett Cooley is wanted on a bench warrant after not appearing Thursday in Jones County Circuit Court.

According to the sheriff’s department, Cooley is charged with trafficking of a controlled substance, methamphetamine, as a habitual offender and was scheduled to stand trial beginning Thursday.

Anyone with information about Cooley’s whereabouts is asked to contact the Jones County Sheriff’s Department at 601-425-3147.

Tipsters may also call Jones County Crime Stoppers at 601-428-STOP and could be eligible for a financial reward if the information leads to Cooley’s arrest.

item.title: Harrison County Deputies Intercept $25K IRS Scam, Save Elderly Victim From Further Loss - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HARRISON COUNTY — Investigators with the Harrison County Sheriff’s Office intercepted $25,000 in cash tied to an IRS scam targeting an elderly woman, preventing additional financial losses, Sheriff Matt Haley announced Thursday.

Authorities said the woman had been instructed to mail the cash as payment for what she believed were outstanding tax obligations. The package was stopped at a local shipping business in Long Beach after an alert clerk became suspicious of the transaction.

According to the sheriff’s office, the woman entered Premier Postal to send a poorly packaged parcel while speaking on the phone with a man who had a strong foreign accent and was directing her on shipping procedures. While assisting her, the clerk discovered the package contained a large amount of cash and grew concerned when the woman could not explain the recipient or justify the high cost of expedited shipping.

The woman left the business before the package was sent, prompting the clerk, who had recently seen public warnings about scams issued by the sheriff’s office, to contact investigators.

Deputies located the woman at her home, where she and a relative told investigators the payment was intended for the IRS to avoid arrest and additional penalties. Authorities determined the demand was fraudulent and part of a scam commonly targeting elderly victims.

Investigators also learned the woman had previously sent more than $30,000 to scammers.

The $25,000 package was recovered and returned to the victim. Officials said the clerk’s quick thinking and awareness prevented further losses and provided valuable evidence in the case.

The Department of Homeland Security is assisting in the investigation, which remains ongoing.

Sheriff Haley urged residents to remain vigilant, emphasizing that law enforcement and government agencies will never call to demand immediate payment, particularly in cash.

Officials encourage anyone who suspects a scam or believes someone may be a victim to contact local law enforcement.

item.title: Hancock County authorities searching for armed aggravated assault suspect - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HANCOCK COUNTY — Authorities in Hancock County are asking for the public’s help in locating a man wanted for aggravated assault who is considered armed and dangerous.

The Hancock County Sheriff’s Office is searching for Gavin J. Victor Ladner, 31, of Saucier, who fled the scene of an incident in the Crane Creek community, according to officials.

Investigators said Ladner’s vehicle has since been recovered in neighboring Harrison County, but he remains at large. Authorities warned that he may still be in possession of a shotgun.

Officials are urging anyone who sees Ladner or knows his immediate whereabouts to call Central Dispatch at 228-255-9191 or dial 911.

Those with non-emergency information about Ladner’s possible whereabouts are also encouraged to contact dispatch or submit anonymous tips through the sheriff’s office website or mobile app.

Authorities cautioned residents not to rely on social media comments to report information, noting that such posts can be difficult to monitor in real time.

Ladner should not be approached, officials said.

item.title: DeSoto County DA seeks no bond for Horn Lake shooting suspect, files additional charge - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HORN LAKE – The DeSoto County District Attorney’s Office is seeking no bond for a Horn Lake man accused in a shooting earlier this week at Discount Market on Goodman Road.

District Attorney Matthew Barton announced that his office has filed a petition asking the court to deny bond for 22-year-old Taderius Young of Horn Lake following the shooting.

Young was taken into custody and charged with aggravated assault in connection with the incident. He is being held at the DeSoto County Adult Detention Center.

In addition to the aggravated assault charge, prosecutors said Young has also been charged with auto burglary in a separate case. The district attorney’s office said that charge stemmed from a case previously secured through a secret indictment in February.

According to the filing, the state argues that Young poses a special danger to the community under Article 3, Section 29 of the Mississippi Constitution and should be held without bond.

“Young has made it abundantly clear that our community isn’t safe without him in custody,” Barton said. “That is why we are asking the court to deny his bond and keep him exactly where he belongs, behind bars.”

Barton said his office plans to pursue every legal avenue available to hold violent offenders accountable.

“Let this be a message to violent criminals,” Barton said. “We don’t play here. If you bring violence into our community, we will find you, we will charge you, and, as Young is about to find out, we are going to aggressively prosecute you.”

The case was investigated by the Horn Lake Police Department.

item.title: Brandon to Host Annual Crawfish Crawl 5K, Festival - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BRANDON — The Brandon Main Street Association will host its fourth annual Crawfish Crawl 5K and post-race festival on Saturday, April 18, bringing hundreds of runners and visitors to downtown Brandon.

Organizers said more than 250 participants have already registered for the event, with runners traveling from across Mississippi as well as neighboring states, including Florida and Louisiana. The event serves as a fundraiser for the association while also boosting local businesses by drawing visitors to shop and dine throughout the day.

The 5K race will begin at 8 a.m. and wind through downtown Brandon, followed by the New Little Crawlers one-mile run at 8:30 a.m.

A finish-line celebration will take place at Genna Benna’s, featuring breakfast, drinks and live music. Later in the day, the Crawfish Crawl Festival will be held from 10:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Mudbugs042, offering crawfish, live entertainment and crawfish races.

Organizers said the event has become a community-wide effort, with residents lining the race route to cheer on participants, creating a lively, family-friendly atmosphere.

item.title: Two wanted after man shot in Horn Lake McDonalds parking lot - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HORN LAKE – Horn Lake police are searching for two suspects after a man was shot during an assault in a McDonald’s parking lot last month.

According to police, officers responded March 26, 2026, to a report of a suspicious person in the parking lot of the McDonald’s at 4170 Fountain Lane. When officers arrived, they found a male victim lying in the parking lot with a gunshot wound to his upper shoulder.

Emergency medical personnel transported the man to a hospital for treatment, and he was later released.

Investigators said the victim had been jumped by several people in the parking lot. During the confrontation, two people who initially approached the victim pulled out a handgun, and during a brief struggle, one of them fired a shot that struck the man in the shoulder.

Horn Lake investigators said they were able to identify several people involved in the assault.

Police said warrants have been issued for 22-year-old Markevion Williams on charges of aggravated assault with a weapon and felony conspiracy to commit a crime. A warrant also has been issued for 20-year-old Morgan Williams on a charge of felony conspiracy to commit a crime.

Anyone with information about the whereabouts of Markevion Williams or Morgan Williams is asked to contact the Horn Lake Police Department at 662-393-6174.

item.title: Sheriff: "Armed and dangerous" suspect wanted in Natchez shooting investigation - Darkhorse Press

ADAMS COUNTY – The Adams County Sheriff’s Office has identified a suspect in a shots fired investigation Thursday and said two people who were initially detained have since been released.

The investigation stems from a shooting reported earlier in the area of Martin Luther King Jr. Street and Broadmoor Drive, according to the sheriff’s office.

Officials described Johnson as armed and dangerous and told the public not to approach him.

The sheriff’s office also warned that anyone found harboring, concealing or assisting Johnson could face criminal charges.

This is an active investigation.

item.title: Oxford police make arrests in separate intimidation, burglary cases - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
OXFORD – Oxford police have made arrests in two separate cases involving alleged threats and a domestic disturbance, according to the Oxford Police Department.

In the first case, officers responded Dec. 2, 2025, to a report of threats made on social media at an apartment complex on Anderson Road.

After an investigation, police arrested 24-year-old Jordan Rupert of West Point and charged him with cyberstalking, email threats and harassment. Authorities said Rupert was arrested in Clay County on a warrant from another jurisdiction, and a hold was placed on him in the Oxford case.

Rupert later appeared before a municipal court judge for an initial bond hearing. Police thanked the Clay County Sheriff’s Office for its assistance.

In the second case, officers responded March 20, 2026, to a domestic disturbance involving multiple people at an apartment complex near Private Road 3151.

Following an investigation, police charged 46-year-old Shaun Thomas of Oxford with burglary of a dwelling.

Thomas was transported to the Lafayette County Detention Center and later appeared before a municipal court judge for an initial bond hearing.

item.title: Mississippi Museum of Natural Science to host NatureFEST on April 11 in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks and its Mississippi Museum of Natural Science will host the annual “NatureFEST!” event April 11, offering a full day of outdoor-themed activities for visitors of all ages.

The event is scheduled from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the museum, located in LeFleur’s Bluff State Park. Organizers describe NatureFEST as a combination of a festival, nature outing and museum experience designed to encourage exploration and hands-on learning.

Visitors can expect live animal encounters, demonstrations, and opportunities to interact with museum scientists, along with a variety of outdoor activities throughout the day.

“NatureFEST is one of our favorite days of the year,” Museum Director Angel Rohnke said. “It is an incredible opportunity for families to connect with Mississippi’s natural world in fun, memorable ways and to see firsthand how science, conservation, and discovery all come together here at the Museum.”

Activities will include animal presentations from Wild Acres, Freedom Ranch and the Hattiesburg Zoo, fish feedings in the museum’s aquariums, and access to exhibits such as “Giants of the Ice Age.” Guests can also take part in interactive programs, watch artist Ellen Langford at work and meet author Kay Meadows.

The event will also feature plant sales from Camp Creek Native Plants, local vendors and food trucks, including Skenny Burgers, Gator’s and Mo’Betta Desserts. Food and vendor purchases are not included with admission.

Admission to NatureFEST is included with regular museum entry or a Mississippi Museum of Natural Science Foundation membership. General admission is $9 for adults, $7 for youth ages 3 to 18 and $8 for seniors ages 60 and older.

The day will begin with the Buffalo Peak Outfitters Hoka 5K Hike/Run, which requires registration and includes admission to NatureFEST.

The Mississippi Museum of Natural Science is located at 2148 Riverside Drive in Jackson and offers exhibits and programs focused on the state’s natural heritage year-round.

item.title: Memphis man gets more than 14 years in federal prison for kidnapping - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
OXFORD — A Memphis man has been sentenced to more than 14 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to kidnapping a woman in Southaven, authorities said.

Elmer Smith, 39, of Memphis, Tennessee, was sentenced by Senior U.S. District Court Judge Michael P. Mills to 170 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release. He was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service after sentencing.

According to court documents, Smith traveled from Memphis to Southaven on Feb. 15, 2024, in search of the victim, with whom he had an intimate relationship. Authorities said he located her at her workplace, assaulted her and forced her into his vehicle before taking her back to Memphis without her consent.

The victim was later located by the Memphis Police Department, which arrested Smith a short time after the abduction.

U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary said the crime would not be tolerated.

“Such conduct is unconscionable and will not be tolerated in our district,” Leary said in a statement, adding that those who travel to Mississippi to commit crimes “will be caught, prosecuted and jailed.”

Robert Eikhoff, special agent in charge of the FBI Jackson Field Office, said the sentence sends a clear message that violent acts will be prosecuted.

“There is no excuse for the abuse or the profound trauma inflicted on the victim,” Eikhoff said, adding that the FBI will continue working with law enforcement partners to hold offenders accountable.

Authorities credited the Southaven Police Department and the Memphis Police Department for their work on the case.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Philip Levy and Robert Mims.

item.title: Jackson police chief to host community meetings across city in April, May - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Jackson Police Chief Dr. RaShall Brackney will continue a series of community meetings across Jackson in April and May, inviting residents to share concerns and help shape public safety efforts citywide.

The meetings follow outreach that began in February, when Brackney met with residents, business owners and faith leaders in Wards 5 and 6 to discuss neighborhood priorities and ways the Jackson Police Department can strengthen partnerships with the community.

The next round of meetings will expand to remaining wards through a mix of evening gatherings and daytime outreach events.

Each meeting will include remarks from Brackney, an overview of current public safety initiatives and an open listening session for residents to ask questions, voice concerns and offer ideas.

“I want every neighborhood in Jackson to know that their voice matters and that their police department is listening,” Brackney said. “These meetings are a chance for me to sit down with residents where they live, worship and work, to hear directly about what’s working, what isn’t, and how we can move forward to make every part of this city safer.”

Upcoming meetings are scheduled for April 14 at the Georgetown Event Center, April 16 at Christ United Church, April 30 at Stronger Hope Church, May 1 at Union Station and May 5 at the South Jackson Community Center.

Residents are encouraged to attend the meeting in their ward or any session that fits their schedule.

item.title: Inmate found dead at Marshall County Correctional Facility - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MARSHALL COUNTY – An investigation is underway after an inmate was found dead at the Marshall County Correctional Facility, according to WMC Action News 5. The Mississippi Department of Corrections said 53-year-old Alexander Davis was found dead April 6.

MDOC did not say where inside the facility Davis was found. The agency said the cause and manner of death are pending a full autopsy.

WMC reported Davis was serving a 20-year sentence for selling methamphetamine in a Neshoba County case from 2022. He had been expected to be released in October 2040.

The Marshall County Correctional Facility is located in Holly Springs and can house up to 1,000 inmates, according to WMC.

item.title: Fugitive Returned to Neshoba County to Face 18 Felony Charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
Written by: Mackenzie Joiner

PHILADELPHIA – A man wanted on multiple felony charges in Neshoba County is now back in custody.

According to the Neshoba County Sheriff’s Department, Reginald Triplett returned to the Neshoba County Detention Facility after his arrest out of state. Authorities took him into custody in Cleveland, Ohio, just a few weeks ago. Today, he arrived at the detention facility at approximately 2:00 p.m.

Previously, Queen City Newsfeed reported that Triplett was arrested in Ohio on March 27, 2026 . Since then, officials have worked to bring him back to Mississippi.

Officials say USTE/Global Solutions, a private prisoner transport company, handled the transfer.

Earlier, Triplett faced 18 felony charges issued through the Neshoba County Circuit Court. After his arrest by the U.S. Marshals Service in Ohio, officials arranged his return.

Meanwhile, Sheriff Eric Clark stressed that deputies will continue to track down those who try to avoid arrest.

“Anyone attempting to evade charges or avoid court will be located and returned to face justice,” Clark said. “We will use all available resources to make that happen.”

Now, Triplett remains in custody at the Neshoba County Detention Facility. He will wait there until his court proceedings begin.

As with all criminal cases, Triplett is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

COLUMBUS – A Columbus man has been arrested in connection with an alleged incident involving a minor that police say happened about five years ago on Main Street.

The Columbus Police Department said officers arrested 39-year-old Alvie Jordan on April 8, 2026.

Following an investigation, Jordan was charged with statutory rape in connection with an alleged incident in the 2400 block of Main Street.

Authorities said the case began after the victim recently came forward to report the incident. Police said the victim told investigators she had previously been threatened, which contributed to the delay in reporting.

Jordan was taken into custody without incident and transported to the Lowndes County Adult Detention Center, where he is being held on a $250,000 bond.

Because of the sensitive nature of the case and to protect the identity of the victim, police said no additional information would be released at this time.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with additional information is asked to contact the Columbus Police Department or Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
OXFORD – A Hattiesburg man has been arrested in connection with an Oxford investigation into the alleged sexual assault of a minor, according to the Oxford Police Department.

Police said an investigator was notified March 13, 2026, by Child Protective Services about a possible sexual assault involving a minor.

After an investigation, authorities arrested 71-year-old Auster Porter of Hattiesburg and charged him with sexual battery.

Police said Porter was taken into custody by the Hattiesburg Police Department and then transported to the Lafayette County Detention Center.

He later appeared before a municipal court judge for an initial bond hearing.

The Oxford Police Department thanked the Hattiesburg Police Department for assisting in the case.
